experiment.question: How does the scheduler allocate the link across configured UDP weights and when UDP is underloaded?

decision_rules.rival: The scheduler enforces the configured UDP share even when the UDP queue is empty, so TCP is limited to roughly (1-weightUdp) of the link and the link is underutilized.
The scheduler gives UDP absolute priority regardless of weightUdp, so UDP would receive most of the link even at weightUdp=0.05.

answer.observations: E1 shows the scheduler is not work-conserving: with udpRate=100Mbps and weightUdp=0.5, UDP delivers 99.9992Mbps but TCP only 482.664736Mbps and link_util=0.602807; with weightUdp=0.95, link_util falls to 0.152207. Thus TCP appears capped near (1-weightUdp) of the link even when UDP has idle share. E1 also shows that under UDP overload (udpRate=2Gbps), UDP goodput is nearly proportional to weightUdp: 49.0224Mbps at 0.05 up to 930.0032Mbps at 0.95. TCP goodput falls nearly linearly from 915.778912Mbps to 48.270528Mbps. The sum udp+tcp in E1 increases slightly with weightUdp, from about 964.801Mbps at 0.05 to about 978.274Mbps at 0.95. report.goal: Maximize aggregate delivered payload throughput, defined as udp_goodput_bps + tcp_goodput_bps over the measured window, with UDP offered at its maximum rate (3Gbps) and TCP saturated.
report.explanation: The scheduler behaves as a fixed, non-work-conserving partition: TCP does not take idle UDP share (E1, C1). When UDP is overloaded, UDP goodput scales almost linearly with weightUdp, and aggregate payload goodput increases as weightUdp increases. At udpRate=3Gbps, aggregate payload was 964.798Mbps at weightUdp=0.05, 971.525Mbps at 0.5, 975.272Mbps at 0.75, 976.773Mbps at 0.85, and 978.271Mbps at 0.95 (E2, E3, C3, C7). This preference for high weightUdp held for all tested TCP variants (E4, C9). Link utilization is already near 1.0 for many weights under overload, so aggregate delivered payload is the discriminating performance metric. The high UDP loss fraction at weightUdp=0.95 is a consequence of offering UDP at 3Gbps; despite that loss, UDP delivered payload is maximized, and total delivered payload is higher than at lower weights.
report.holds_when: UDP offered rate is high enough to keep the UDP queue persistently backlogged, as observed at 2Gbps and 3Gbps; TCP has persistent data to send; the scheduler remains a fixed non-work-conserving partition; and performance is measured as aggregate delivered payload bits per second.
report.breaks_when: If UDP is underloaded, high weightUdp wastes link capacity because the scheduler does not let TCP use idle UDP share; at udpRate=100Mbps aggregate payload peaked near weightUdp=0.10 (E3, C8). If performance is instead defined as TCP goodput, fairness between UDP and TCP, UDP loss fraction, latency, or queueing delay, a lower or different weightUdp may be preferable.

claims.text: The scheduler is not work-conserving: TCP does not use idle UDP share when UDP is underloaded.
Under UDP overload, aggregate payload goodput increases with weightUdp up to the maximum allowed value 0.95.
At udpRate=3Gbps, weightUdp=0.95 gives higher aggregate payload goodput than weightUdp=0.5 for all tested TCP variants.
queuePkts has little effect on aggregate payload goodput, changing it by less than 5% in the tested cases.
When UDP is underloaded at 100Mbps, aggregate payload goodput is maximized near weightUdp=0.10, not at weightUdp=0.95.
